html:
SMTO-GWT-0090 — The Gateway is waiting for a data cleanup to finish

GUID: df8e57f2-aabf-5019-8479-935308a505d8
Slug: gateway-runtime-purge-pending
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Someone started deleting old runtime data on the server and its Gateways. Until that cleanup finishes on this Gateway, it refuses new work. This request was not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Data › Storage and look at the progress of the runtime data purge for this Gateway. The Gateway takes new work only after the cleanup there is complete.
  2. If the cleanup shows as partial or blocked, select Retry pending targets. A Gateway that was offline or busy during the cleanup may need it to run again.
  3. When the cleanup shows completed, select Check connection for this Gateway in Settings › Setup › Gateways, then send your request again. The refused request never ran, so sending it again is safe once the cleanup is done.

What success looks like

  • Settings › Data › Storage shows the purge as completed, and your request runs on the Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start another purge while this one is unfinished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected an ordinary request during authentication because its runtime purge journal shows a cleanup that has not completed.

What this means

  • The Gateway rejected dispatch while runtime cleanup is pending. The classification describes only the condition observed by the producer.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway dispatch is rejected while a purge admission fence is active.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check the purge status in Settings › Data › Storage (or the Gateway's /runtime-purge status); the request was rejected before dispatch with gateway_runtime_purge_pending. Wait for the operation to reach completed, or use Retry pending targets if it is partial or blocked, then prepare a new request. Requests from before the purge also need the new runtime epoch.
  • Wait for the existing cleanup operation to complete or inspect its status before preparing new Gateway work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
